references.text: The Lord had previously promised to give the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that they would not leave Egypt empty-handed.
The fulfillment of the promise that the Lord gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that they gave them what they asked for.
A similar expression is used regarding Joseph, where the Lord gave him favor in the eyes of the prison guards.
Esther also found favor in the eyes of all who saw her, just as the Israelites found favor with the Egyptians.
Stephen refers to how God gave Moses favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, confirming Moses' greatness in Egypt.
The description of Moses' greatness and the mighty deeds he performed in Egypt, seen by all Israel.
Moses is described as the most humble man on earth, which contrasts with his great standing in Egypt.
Highlights the theological progression from the Egyptians' goodwill (11:3) to their fear and recognition of the Lord's power (14:31).
Creates a theological contrast between God's gift of goodwill (11:3) and His decision to harden Pharaoh's heart (14:4).
A clear typological parallel: God's presence makes both Joseph and Moses men who find favor with the Egyptians.
